title: The Meme Economy: How Online Humor Rewrites Punjab Kings’s Story
dek: Online humour feeds on collapses and thrashings. The data cannot read the jokes about Punjab Kings, but it can count the moments that tend to start them.
excerpt: Punjab Kings have suffered heavy defeats and sub-120 totals, the raw material of online mockery. How those moments are retold is a question about fans, not scorecards.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

They have been bowled out or held under 120 in {{ev:me-low}} innings of ten overs or more.

sections.heading: The Raw Material of Memes
body: Online humour about a team tends to start from the same moments: collapses, thrashings and scorelines that are easy to screenshot.
The CricField warehouse holds no survey, sentiment or social-media data, so it cannot measure what fans feel. It can measure what they have watched.

sections.heading: Counting the Bad Days
body: {{ev:me-hv}} of Punjab Kings' defeats were heavy, {{ev:me-hvpct}} of all their losses, by forty runs or more or with thirty balls or more to spare.
They have been held under 120 in {{ev:me-low}} innings of ten overs or more; the lowest was {{ev:me-lowest}}, in {{ev:me-lowest-y}}. The chart counts both by season.

sections.heading: Rewriting the Story
body: Memes compress a season into one image. A single collapse can define how a team is talked about long after a strong run of results.

sections.heading: Owning the Joke
body: Some franchises lean into self-deprecating humour; others ignore it. Which approach protects the brand is not something match data can show.
Testing it would need social-media sentiment data around specific matches.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Bad Days Are Rare but Memorable
body: Heavy defeats make up a measurable minority of Punjab Kings' losses. Their weight in the online story is likely far larger than their share of results.
That gap is the meme economy, and it needs sentiment data to measure.

methodology: CricField holds ball-by-ball cricket data and no fan survey, sentiment or social-media data. This article measures the cricket fans have experienced; statements about fans themselves are labelled hypotheses. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Heavy defeat = lost by forty runs or more, or with thirty balls or more to spare. Low totals count innings of at least ten overs.
